🔴 NEEDS DECISION, verbatim from the readme fact-check 2026-09-08, and it PAUSES the readme surface under the GATE 4 pre-authorisation: 'The README says the command-line tool makes zero network calls, and that is true of the engine's own code - check [9] proves it and no update check exists. But the engine spawns tools that reach the network under their own settings: section 24 runs `winget list`, which refreshes its sources from cdn.winget.microsoft.com when they are older than 15 minutes and emits Microsoft telemetry by default; section 22 runs `npm root -g` and --purge-all runs `npm cache clean --force`, and npm's update notifier fetches npm@latest from the registry at most once a day unless update-notifier=false; section 1 runs `pnpm store prune` inside the DEFAULT SAFE BATCH, and pnpm's own update check is unverified. A firewall log during `windowsweep --profile audit` would show winget talking to Microsoft.' OPTIONS: (a) RECOMMENDED - keep every README fence as written, because they describe the tool and are true of it, and add one disclosed sentence to docs/safety-model.md and the FAQ via the docs-safety and docs-help surfaces: 'The tools it runs for you keep their own habits: winget and npm may check their own sources and send their own telemetry; the engine itself never does.' (b) add that clause to the README's S-031 as well. (c) treat child-process behaviour as out of scope and record the reasoning, so it is a decision rather than an oversight. Any of the three keeps Bible section 3's commitment 3 true and none requires inventing a fact.

🔴 FIVE NEEDS DECISION lines from the docs-safety fact-check, 2026-09-08 - that surface is NOT safe to apply and needs a round 4. In short: (1) S-004's 'every deletion of anything on your machine passes through one function' is false for seven sections that delete through an external Windows or Docker command (5, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20) and for --uninstall-data; scope it to what the tool removes with its own code. (2) S-015's Configuration cell says 'Nothing is removed' while section 15 removes hiberfil.sys - the --dry-run precedent gives 'nothing OF YOURS is removed'. (3) S-024 and Bible 3.2 say a dry-run writes 'two files of its own'; the page's own recommended command writes three, and sections 17, 22, 24, 25 each add one. (4) The Rebuilds tier's 'a cache comes back' is false for cleanmgr's Previous Installations and Device Driver Packages, DISM's superseded components and crash dumps. (5) The live safety-model exclusions section needs a slot. Each touches a GATE 1 or GATE 2 artefact or the catalogue's tier names, so none is the writer's to take.

Engine defect found by the docs-safety fact-check 2026-09-08, filed not fixed: `--scan` ignores `--developer` / `--not-developer`. Resolve-DeveloperMode runs only for walkthrough, menu, all and only (windowsweep.ps1:300), so in scan mode $ws.Developer stays $null and section 0 prints 'Developer mode: not decided yet' whatever the flag says. The DESKTOP passes those flags to --scan (desktop/src/lib/engine.ts:135) and the engine ignores them there, so the --json `developer` field is null on every scan the window makes.
notes: The completion run opened 2026-09-07 under the plan at ../completion-plan-2026-09-07.md. GATE 4 is pre-authorised for the eleven remaining surfaces on a stated condition (gate4PreAuthorised), so a session applies an approved surface without stopping - but a finalizer FAIL or a fresh NEEDS DECISION still pauses that one surface. RED Two defects were found in copy this system had already approved: splash.html promises that the updater checks for a newer build and NOTHING in the app ever called the updater, and tauri.conf.json carried a plugins.updater.dialog key the plugin does not accept. Both were found by grepping for the mechanism rather than for the words, which is the sharpened form of the 2026-09-05 clause about approved artefacts holding claims nobody re-reads. RED And the story lint hook is blind to copy inside a code fence, so on the slot-shaped surfaces - cli-strings, and any .tsx copy - the fact-checker and a human reader are the only real gate; a green hook there is not evidence. | 2026-09-07 later: the analytics opt-out was removed by the owner mid-run, which re-opened a recorded surface - the first time that has happened here. The handling worth repeating: the words were changed in the CLICK DUMMY first and the reason written into the design README beside them (section 10a), so the person who reads the dummy to approve it sees why it changed; only then did the app follow. The voice decision inside that change was to KEEP the "Never sent" list against an instruction to keep it to one line, because band R delivers reassurance as a specific refusal and a notice with nothing checkable in it is an announcement. 🔴 And the cli-strings writer PROVED the fenced-copy blindness on its own file rather than citing the precedent: two banned words inside a slot fence went undetected (exit 0), the same two words in the commentary were both named (exit 2). That is a reproducible two-command proof and it belongs in the global record.

gate4PreAuthorised.condition: The finalizer's fact-consistency check PASSES and the surface carries zero unanswered NEEDS DECISION. Either one failing stops THAT surface only: the question goes verbatim into openDecisions below and into docs/MANUAL-TASKS.md the turn it arrives, and the run moves to the next surface rather than guessing.

You grant GATE 4 in advance for all eleven, conditional on the finalizer's fact-consistency PASS and zero unanswered NEEDS DECISION. Opus applies each surface to the real files and re-mirrors the docs site; a new NEEDS DECISION pauses only that surface.
